validity.researcher_notes: EXISTENCE: CONFIRMED real. The GEM row's sole cited source is one Arabic article (attaqa.net / AlTaqa, 2023-09-17) which every value cell reuses. That article DOES name the field and describe the pipeline, and I found an INDEPENDENT second source: Egypt Oil & Gas ('Agiba to pump $500M during FY2024/25') states Agiba is 'extending another line from the Faramid field to Badr El Din Company to process 24 mcf/d of natural gas from the field's production.' The field itself is well documented as Eni/Agiba's 'Faramid'/'Faramid South' discovery in the East Obayed concession (~30 km NW of the Meleiha concession, Western Desert), a 2018 gas find opened to production at ~25 MMscf/d, brought online Sept 2023. Two independent origins (attaqa + Egypt Oil & Gas) => existence high. NOTE the GEM name is misspelled 'Framid'; correct Latin transliteration is 'Faramid' (Arabic فراميد). CLASSIFICATION: it is a ~38 km, 10-in single-field connector line moving Faramid's produced gas to the Badr El Din (BAPETCO) processing facility. That is functionally a field-to-plant feeder, borderline gathering rather than a true transmission trunk, BUT this matches GEM's and GulfPub's consistent treatment of Western Desert field-connector lines (cf. P3937/P3938 Badr El Din spurs, P6693 Salam spurline, GulfPub 'Meleiha-Marsa Matruh' 10-in, 'Khepri-Salam' 12-in) as operating pipelines, so no hard classification concern is raised. DUPLICATE: none. No roster row references Faramid or Agiba as this pipe. The auto-suggested GulfPub match 'Western Desert Gas Project - Tarek Spur' (10-in, 14 km, Ras Kanayes 4 -> Tarek field, operator Khalda/KPC) is a DIFFERENT field, operator and length (14 vs 38 km) - not a duplicate. No GulfPub feature names Faramid. ATTRIBUTION: Operator 'Agiba Petroleum Co' CONFIRMED (Agiba = the Eni-IEOC + EGPC operating JV); its Operator [ref] cell was blank and is now filled. Delivery point Badr El Din is a BAPETCO facility (delivery endpoint, not the operator). Fuel=Gas, PipelineType=transmission, Status=operating all supported. SPEC: capacity 25 MMcf/d (attaqa) vs 24 mcf/d processed (Egypt Oil & Gas) - two sources in close agreement => high. Length 38 km and diameter 10 in appear only in the attaqa article (single source) => medium, no contradicting source found. Start 2023 supported (production began Sept 2023). No material disagreement anywhere, so verdict is confirmed with caveats, not a concern.

routes.corridor_desc: Short (~38 km) intra-field trunk in the northern Egyptian Western Desert. The Faramid/Faramid South field sits in the East Obayed concession, described by the operator as ~30 km northwest of the Meleiha concession. The line runs from that field to the Badr El Din (BAPETCO) processing company/plant, which handles the produced gas (~24-25 MMcf/d). Bound is only concession-scale: both endpoints are defensibly within the Matruh-governorate Western Desert oil/gas belt (the Obayed-Meleiha-Badr El Din cluster southwest of Alexandria/Marsa Matruh), but no published coordinates or route trace was found, so exact endpoint lat/lon are left null rather than invented.
routes.researcher_notes: Endpoints established from sources, not the blank GEM cells: attaqa says Agiba laid a 10-in / 38-km line to connect Faramid to the production network; Egypt Oil & Gas names the destination as 'Badr El Din Company' (the BAPETCO processing facility). Eni/Agiba locate Faramid in the East Obayed concession ~30 km NW of Meleiha. No coordinates published; endpoint lat/lon left null (no fabrication). Corridor bound is concession-scale only, hence suggested_route_accuracy=low.
